summary: Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD under Karl Hoffmann and his Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where he was an assistant before holding a chair at Regensburg (1983–2006).

Geshe Bel-den-drak-ba is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi (attested 1988).

Geshe Gendün Lodrö worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his Geshe degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Ngawang Lekden. He served on the faculty at Drepung Gomang, taught at the University of Hamburg (1967), and visited the University of Virginia (~1979).

Geshe Jampa Tegchok was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1992) and resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha (~1993–1998).
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. His career includes posts at Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987) and Sera Monastery (attested 1992).

Geshe Kelsang Gyatso studied at Jampa Ling, Tashilhunpo, Ngamring Chöde, and Sera Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche. A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, he taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre from 1977 and founded the New Kadampa Tradition in 1991.

Geshe Lhakdor studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery. Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he worked at Tibet House, New Delhi (1986–1989), and became Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 2005.

Geshe Lhundub Sopa studied at Gaden Chokhor and Sera Monastery. Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he joined the University of Wisconsin-Madison faculty in 1967, becoming full professor in 1985, and founded the Deer Park Buddhist Center in 1976.

Geshe Lobsang Gyatso studied at Drepung Monastery, working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics in 1973, serving as its director until 1997, and founded the College for Higher Tibetan Studies in 1991.

Educated at Drepung Monastery, Geshe Lobsang Tenzin worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He headed CST Dalhousie (1965–1970), directed the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1988–2001), and served as Chancellor of Sanchi University of Buddhist-Indic Studies.
Geshe Lobsang Tharchin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Lharampa Geshe degree at Sera Mey Monastery by 1953 and also studied at Gyume Tantric College.

Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 2010, he was attested as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics and held a post at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Geshe Ngawang Nyima was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Drepung Monastery (attested 1966 and 1976), Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1995), and Leiden University.
Geshe Palden Dragpa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Tibet House, New Delhi, where he served as librarian (attested 1987–1992) and was also attested in 2004.

Geshe Rabten studied at Sera Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche. Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1969–1974) and founded Rabten Choeling, Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg, Tashi Rabten, and Gephel Ling.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. Focusing on Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he served as resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives starting in 1978.

Geshe Tashi Tsering studied at Sera and Gyuto Monasteries under Geshe Thubten Rinchen. A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, he held posts at Kopan Monastery and Gandhi Foundation College (~1992–1994) before becoming resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre in 1994.
Geshe Tsondru Kongpel is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed Geshe studies at both Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Wangyal studied at Drepung Monastery under Agvan Dorjiev. Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he founded the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center in 1958, leading it until 1983, and taught at Columbia University (~1962–1974).

Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, where he was attested in 1991, 2004, and from 2014 to 2019.
